toc.title: Serverless, hybrid, load balancing and practice

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Choose among On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances and Spot
  • Design Spot workloads that survive interruptions
  • Right-size with instance families, sizes, Graviton and Compute Optimizer
  • Pick scaling, hibernation, serverless and container options that cut cost
  • Choose a load balancer and an availability level that match the workload class

2Purchasing options, Spot and right-sizing

Running case

Lantern and Loom Trims the Compute Bill

  • The web tier runs 24 hours a day at a steady baseline, with spikes at sales
  • Nightly image processing can be restarted if it stops
  • Test servers sit idle evenings and weekends
  • Large instances run at 10% CPU
  • Each team runs its own load balancer: cut the compute bill

EC2 Purchasing Options

Option Commitment Best for
On-Demand None, pay per second Short, unpredictable or new workloads
Savings Plans $ per hour, 1 or 3 years Steady usage, with flexibility
Reserved Instances A specific configuration, 1 or 3 years Steady usage that will not change
Spot Instances None; can be interrupted Fault-tolerant, flexible work, up to 90% off
  • Dedicated Hosts and Capacity Reservations serve licensing and capacity, not price

Exam tip: Steady baseline: commit. Spiky or new: On-Demand. Restartable work: Spot.

Savings Plans and Reserved Instances

Type Saves up to Flexibility
Compute Savings Plans 66% Any family, size, OS, tenancy, Region; also Fargate and Lambda
EC2 Instance Savings Plans 72% One family in one Region; any size, OS, tenancy
Standard Reserved Instances 72% One configuration; can be sold on the RI Marketplace
Convertible Reserved Instances 66% Can be exchanged by hand
  • Payment: All, Partial or No upfront; terms cannot be cancelled
  • Savings Plans give no capacity reservation and do not cover Spot

Exam tip: Most flexibility: Compute Savings Plans. Deepest discount for one family: EC2 Instance plan.

Layering Purchase Options

  • Bottom layer: the minimum you always use: Savings Plans or RIs
  • Middle layer: predictable peaks: On-Demand
  • Top layer: restartable bursts: Spot
  • Never commit to the peak: unused commitment is still billed

Exam tip: Commit to the floor of your usage, not the ceiling.

Spot Instances Done Right

Practice Why
Stateless, fault-tolerant work Batch, CI/CD, containers, big data, rendering, stateless web
Be flexible across instance types and AZs More capacity pools to draw from
Use an Auto Scaling group or EC2 Fleet with the price-capacity-optimized strategy Picks available, low-price pools
Handle the 2-minute interruption notice Checkpoint or drain, using EventBridge
Turn on Capacity Rebalancing Replaces instances at elevated risk early
  • Do not use Spot for stateful or tightly coupled work

Exam tip: Restartable and flexible: Spot. A database or a single critical server: never Spot.

Right-Sizing and Instance Families

Family Optimized for Example use
General purpose (M, T) Balanced CPU and memory; T is burstable Web and app servers, small databases
Compute optimized (C) High CPU Batch, encoding, game servers
Memory optimized (R, X) Large memory In-memory caches and databases
Storage optimized (I, D) High local I/O Data warehouses, NoSQL
Accelerated (P, G) GPUs Machine learning, graphics
  • Graviton (Arm) instances often cost less for the same work
  • Match size to measured use, not to a guess

Exam tip: Instances at 10% CPU are too big: right-size, do not buy more commitment.

Compute Optimizer and Cost Visibility

  • Compute Optimizer reads 14 days of metrics and flags over-provisioned, under-provisioned and optimized resources
  • It covers EC2, Auto Scaling groups, EBS, Lambda, ECS on Fargate and more
  • Enhanced infrastructure metrics (paid) extend the look-back to 93 days
  • Cost Explorer gives rightsizing and Savings Plans recommendations
  • Right-size first, then commit: a plan on oversized instances locks in waste
  • Opt in at the organization level to see all accounts
  • Budgets alert on Savings Plans coverage; cost allocation tags and consolidated billing share commitments; the Cost and Usage Report gives line items

Exam tip: Right-size first, commit second.

Scaling for Cost

Approach Cost effect
Horizontal scaling (add and remove instances) Capacity follows demand; pay only for what runs
Vertical scaling (larger size) A restart is needed; fine for one-off right-sizing
Scheduled scaling Scale in before known quiet periods
Target tracking Holds a metric such as 50% CPU
Stop non-production nights and weekends No instance charge while stopped; EBS still bills
  • Mixed instances groups blend On-Demand and Spot

Exam tip: Idle test servers: schedule them off. Spikes: horizontal scaling, not a larger instance.

3Serverless, hybrid, load balancing and practice

Hibernation and Availability by Workload Class

Workload class Cost-effective availability
Production Multi-AZ (two or more Availability Zones), Auto Scaling, committed baseline
Non-production Single AZ, stopped or scaled to zero off hours
Batch and analytics Spot, restart on interruption
  • Hibernation saves RAM to the encrypted EBS root volume, then stops the instance
  • On start, memory and processes return, so a slow-to-warm app resumes fast
  • No instance charge while hibernated; you pay for EBS storage, including the saved RAM
  • Instances must be enabled for hibernation at launch, with limits on size and days

Exam tip: Stop at night but keep in-memory state: hibernate the instance.

Serverless and Containers

Service You pay for Cost lever
AWS Lambda Requests and duration by memory (GB-seconds) Set memory by testing; Arm (Graviton) costs less per millisecond
AWS Fargate vCPU and memory per second, no servers Fargate Spot for restartable tasks; right-size task sizes
ECS or EKS on EC2 The instances Pack containers densely; use Spot and Savings Plans
EC2 Instance time Best for steady, high utilization
  • Compute Savings Plans cover EC2, Fargate and Lambda; containers suit microservices

Exam tip: Spiky or idle-most-of-the-day: Lambda or Fargate. Always busy: EC2 with a commitment.

Hybrid, Edge and Licensing

Option Use it when
AWS Outposts AWS infrastructure on premises for low latency or data residency
Local Zones, Wavelength Compute close to users or 5G networks
Edge processing CloudFront Functions, Lambda@Edge cut origin work
License Manager Track license rules and prevent overuse
Dedicated Hosts Bring your own per-socket or per-core licenses
  • Optimize CPUs lowers vCPU count to cut per-core licensing
  • Use hybrid and edge only when a requirement demands it

Exam tip: Do not add Outposts for price: it exists for latency or residency.

Load Balancer Cost Strategy

Balancer Layer Choose it for
Application (ALB) 7 HTTP/HTTPS, host and path rules, many apps on one balancer
Network (NLB) 4 TCP/UDP, static IPs, extreme scale
Gateway Load Balancer 3 Inline firewall and inspection appliances
  • Billing is hourly plus capacity units used
  • Consolidate many apps behind one ALB with host and path rules and separate target groups
  • Delete idle balancers: they bill by the hour
  • A single ALB can send traffic to EC2, containers and Lambda

Exam tip: Each team with its own ALB is the clue: consolidate with host or path routing.

Choosing the Cheapest Compute

  • Steady, always on: Savings Plans or RIs
  • Spiky or new: On-Demand with Auto Scaling
  • Restartable and flexible: Spot
  • Idle most of the day: Lambda or Fargate
  • Idle nights, memory to keep: hibernate

Exam tip: Name the usage pattern first, then pick the cheapest option that tolerates it.

What the Exam Asks: Cost-Optimized Compute

  • Which purchase option fits a steady, spiky or restartable workload
  • Which Savings Plan or RI gives the needed flexibility
  • How to right-size and with which tool
  • Which service is cheapest: EC2, Lambda or Fargate
  • Which load balancer and how to consolidate

Exam tip: Look for the clues: steady, restartable, idle, flexible, on premises, per team.

Design Check: Lantern and Loom Trims the Compute Bill

Requirement Design
Steady 24-hour web tier Compute Savings Plans for the baseline
Sale-day spikes On-Demand through Auto Scaling
Restartable nightly image jobs Spot in a mixed-instances group
Idle test servers Scheduled stop, or hibernate to keep state
10% CPU large instances Compute Optimizer, then right-size or move to Graviton
A load balancer per team One ALB with host and path rules
Commit safely Right-size first, then commit
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Lantern and Loom runs a nightly image-processing job that splits work into many small tasks. The job can restart any task if an instance stops. The team wants the lowest compute cost. Which approach fits?

  • AAn Auto Scaling group with mixed instance types on Spot
  • BA fleet of On-Demand instances covered by a three-year Reserved Instance
  • CA Dedicated Host for the whole month
  • DA single large On-Demand instance that runs all night
Show the answer

Answer: A. Restartable, flexible work suits Spot, up to 90% below On-Demand, and using several instance types gives more capacity pools. A Reserved Instance, a Dedicated Host or one large On-Demand instance pays more for a short nightly job.

S2The Lantern and Loom web tier runs steadily all day. The team may move from C5 to Graviton instances next year, and may later move some services to Fargate. They want a commitment discount without being tied to one family. Which purchase fits?

  • AA Standard Reserved Instance for C5
  • BA Spot request with a high maximum price
  • CAn EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the C5 family
  • DA Compute Savings Plan
Show the answer

Answer: D. Compute Savings Plans apply to any instance family, size, Region and OS, and also to Fargate and Lambda, so a move to Graviton or Fargate keeps the discount. A Standard RI and an EC2 Instance plan are tied to one family, and Spot is not a commitment.

S3Which TWO statements about Spot Instances and Savings Plans are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AA Savings Plan can be cancelled at any time without charge
  • BCompute Savings Plans also apply to Fargate and Lambda usage
  • CA Spot Instance is guaranteed to run for six hours
  • DSavings Plans discount Spot Instance usage
  • EA Spot Instance gets a two-minute interruption notice before reclaim
Show the answer

Answer: B, E. Compute Savings Plans cover Fargate and Lambda as well as EC2, and Spot gives a two-minute notice before it reclaims capacity. Savings Plans cannot be cancelled, Spot has no guaranteed run time, and Savings Plans do not apply to Spot usage.

S4A Lantern and Loom reporting server takes 20 minutes to load data into memory each morning. It is idle every night. The team wants to pay no instance charge overnight and still resume with the memory loaded. What should they do?

  • ATerminate the instance at night and launch a new one each morning
  • BCreate an AMI each night and restore a new instance each morning
  • CHibernate the instance at night and start it in the morning
  • DUse a Spot Instance with a very high maximum price
Show the answer

Answer: C. Hibernation saves memory to the encrypted EBS root volume and stops the instance, so there is no instance charge and memory returns on start. Terminating or restoring an AMI loses the loaded memory, and Spot does not keep state.

S5Several Lantern and Loom instances run at about 10% CPU. The architect wants data-driven size recommendations across all accounts before buying any commitment. What should they use?

  • ABuy a three-year Savings Plan for the current instances
  • BEnable AWS Compute Optimizer for the organization
  • CMove every instance to Spot Instances
  • DRaise the Auto Scaling maximum size
Show the answer

Answer: B. Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization metrics and recommends right-sized or cheaper resources, and it can cover all accounts when opted in from the management account. A commitment on oversized instances locks in waste, and Spot or a larger maximum does not right-size.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Buy commit to the floor with Savings Plans, On-Demand for peaks, Spot for restartable work
Spot flexible types and AZs, price-capacity-optimized, 2-minute notice
Right-size families, sizes, Graviton, Compute Optimizer; then commit
Run less schedule off, hibernate, Lambda or Fargate when idle
Balance consolidate behind one ALB; Outposts only for latency or residency
